cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain was performed without intravenous contrast.
cases.findings: The brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity. No focal mass lesion, hemorrhage, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles are normal in size and configuration. Midline structures are centered. The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear. The visualized posterior fossa is unremarkable.

cases.clinicalIndication: Progressive cognitive decline, rule out neurodegenerative disease
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain was performed without intravenous contrast.
cases.findings: There are mild chronic small-vessel ischemic changes involving the deep white matter bilaterally, more prominent in the periventricular regions. Generalized cerebral volume loss is noted, with prominence of the cortical sulci and ventricular system out of proportion to the patient's age. No focal mass lesion, hemorrhage, or restricted diffusion. Midline structures are centered. The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.
cases.impression:
1. Mild chronic small-vessel ischemic changes.
2. Generalized cerebral volume loss, moderate for age.
cases.recommendation: Clinical correlation for vascular risk factor management recommended.

cases.clinicalIndication: Low back pain, rule out disc herniation
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the lumbosacral spine was performed without intravenous contrast.
cases.findings: Normal lumbar lordosis is maintained. Vertebral body heights and signal intensity are preserved. Disc heights are maintained at all levels. No disc bulge, protrusion, or extrusion. The thecal sac is normal. Neural foramina are patent bilaterally at all levels. The conus medullaris terminates at L1 level and demonstrates normal signal intensity. The visualized soft tissues are unremarkable.
cases.impression: Normal MRI of the lumbosacral spine.

cases.clinicalIndication: Chronic low back pain with left leg radiculopathy
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the lumbosacral spine was performed without intravenous contrast.
cases.findings: Loss of normal lumbar lordosis. Multilevel disc desiccation is noted from L2-L3 through L5-S1. At L4-L5, there is a diffuse disc bulge causing mild thecal sac indentation without significant neural foraminal narrowing. At L5-S1, there is a posterior disc protrusion measuring approximately 4 mm in AP dimension, causing moderate left neural foraminal narrowing with contact of the left L5 nerve root. Mild facet arthropathy is present at L4-L5 and L5-S1. The thecal sac is otherwise normal. The conus medullaris terminates at L1 level and demonstrates normal signal intensity.
cases.impression:
1. Loss of lumbar lordosis.
2. Multilevel disc desiccation.
3. L4-L5 diffuse disc bulge with mild thecal sac indentation.
4. L5-S1 posterior disc protrusion with moderate left neural foraminal narrowing and left L5 nerve root contact.
5. Mild facet arthropathy at L4-L5 and L5-S1.
cases.recommendation: Clinical correlation for left L5 radiculopathy. Consider targeted epidural steroid injection if conservative management fails.

cases.clinicalIndication: Neck pain following motor vehicle accident, rule out disc herniation
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the cervical spine was performed without intravenous contrast.
cases.findings: Normal cervical lordosis is maintained. Vertebral body heights and signal intensity are preserved. Disc heights are maintained at all levels. No disc bulge, protrusion, or extrusion. The cervical cord demonstrates normal signal intensity and caliber. Neural foramina are patent bilaterally at all levels. The visualized soft tissues of the neck are unremarkable.
cases.impression: Normal MRI of the cervical spine.

cases.clinicalIndication: Chronic neck pain with bilateral upper extremity paresthesias
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the cervical spine was performed without intravenous contrast.
cases.findings: Straightening of normal cervical lordosis. Multilevel degenerative changes are noted. At C4-C5, there is a disc osteophyte complex causing mild central canal narrowing and mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing. At C5-C6, there is a disc osteophyte complex causing moderate central canal narrowing and moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing. The cervical cord demonstrates normal signal intensity, though it is closely apposed to the posterior disc osteophyte complex at C5-C6. The visualized soft tissues of the neck are unremarkable.
cases.impression:
1. Straightening of cervical lordosis.
2. C4-C5 disc osteophyte complex with mild central canal and mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
3. C5-C6 disc osteophyte complex with moderate central canal and moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
cases.recommendation: Clinical correlation for cervical spondylosis with possible cervical radiculopathy. Consider EMG/NCS if symptoms progress.

study.studyDescription: MRI Brain with Cervical Spine Screening

cases.clinicalIndication: Headache and neck pain, rule out intracranial and upper cervical pathology
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain was performed without intravenous contrast. Limited screening sequences of the cervical spine were also obtained.
cases.findings:
BRAIN: The brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity. No focal mass lesion, hemorrhage, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles are normal in size and configuration. Midline structures are centered. The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

CERVICAL SPINE SCREENING: Limited evaluation of the visualized cervical spine demonstrates normal alignment. The visualized vertebral bodies maintain normal height and signal intensity. No gross disc herniation is identified on the screening sequences. The cervical cord appears normal in caliber within the limitations of the screening examination.
cases.impression:
1. Normal MRI of the brain.
2. Unremarkable limited cervical spine screening.
cases.screeningLimitation: This is a limited screening examination of the cervical spine. Dedicated cervical spine MRI is recommended if clinical symptoms persist or progress.

cases.exam: MRI Lumbosacral Spine with Whole Spine Screening

study.studyDescription: MRI Lumbosacral Spine with Whole Spine Screening

cases.clinicalIndication: Chronic back pain with multilevel symptoms
cases.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the lumbosacral spine was performed without intravenous contrast. Limited screening sequences of the entire spine were also obtained.
cases.findings:
LUMBOSACRAL SPINE: Loss of normal lumbar lordosis. Multilevel degenerative disc disease is noted. At L3-L4, there is a diffuse disc bulge causing mild thecal sac indentation. At L4-L5, there is a posterior disc protrusion measuring approximately 3 mm causing moderate central canal narrowing. At L5-S1, there is disc desiccation with a small posterior disc protrusion. Mild facet arthropathy is present at L4-L5 and L5-S1. The conus medullaris terminates at L1 level and demonstrates normal signal intensity.

WHOLE SPINE SCREENING: Limited evaluation demonstrates multilevel degenerative changes in the cervical spine. At C5-C6, there is a disc osteophyte complex causing mild central canal narrowing on the screening sequences. The visualized thoracic spine is unremarkable. The visualized spinal cord appears normal in caliber within the limitations of the screening examination.
cases.impression:
1. Loss of lumbar lordosis.
2. Multilevel lumbar degenerative disc disease:
   - L3-L4 diffuse disc bulge with mild thecal sac indentation
   - L4-L5 posterior disc protrusion with moderate central canal narrowing
   - L5-S1 disc desiccation with small posterior disc protrusion
3. Mild facet arthropathy at L4-L5 and L5-S1.
4. Limited cervical spine screening: multilevel degenerative changes with C5-C6 disc osteophyte complex causing mild central canal narrowing.
cases.recommendation: Dedicated cervical spine MRI recommended for detailed evaluation. Clinical correlation for lumbar radiculopathy.
cases.screeningLimitation: This is a limited screening examination of the thoracic and cervical spine. Dedicated imaging is recommended for detailed evaluation.
